chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Whoever extends a waterspout, or a privy, or drives in a stake, or ties up an animal, or digs a well in the path of the Muslims, and thereby something is struck and destroyed, then he is liable for it.”

key_terms.بِئْرًا: a well dug into the ground
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable or responsible for compensation
key_terms.طَرِيقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public pathway used by Muslims
key_terms.مِيزَابًا: a waterspout or drainage outlet projecting outward
key_terms.وَتِدًا: a stake or peg fixed into the ground

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable for damage caused by hazards they place in a public road in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes liability for harm caused by placing hazardous things in public pathways used by Muslims. It underscores the protection of public safety and the obligation to compensate for damage resulting from one’s actions in shared spaces.
